gloss: female proprietor; hostess; lady of the house

definitions.gloss: female proprietor; hostess; lady of the house
definitions.explanation: a woman who owns or runs an establishment such as a shop, inn, or restaurant, or the female head of a household

examples.japanese: {女主人|おんなしゅじん}が{出迎|でむか}えてくれた。
examples.english: The mistress of the house came out to greet us.

examples.japanese: その{旅館|りょかん}の{女主人|おんなしゅじん}はとても{親切|しんせつ}だった。
examples.english: The female proprietor of the inn was very kind.

examples.japanese: {女主人|おんなしゅじん}が{自|みずか}ら{料理|りょうり}を{運|はこ}んできて、{一品|いっぴん}ずつ{丁寧|ていねい}に{説明|せつめい}してくれた。
examples.english: The female proprietor personally brought the dishes and explained each one carefully.

notes:
Used when specifically identifying the owner or head of an establishment or household as a woman. Common in literary contexts and when describing traditional Japanese businesses like {旅館|りょかん} (Japanese inns) or {料亭|りょうてい} (high-end Japanese restaurants).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旅館|りょかん}の{女主人|おんなしゅじん}: the female proprietor of an inn
- {店|みせ}の{女主人|おんなしゅじん}: the female shop owner
- {女主人|おんなしゅじん}が{切|き}り{盛|も}りする: for the female proprietor to run (a business)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {女将|おかみ}: proprietress of a traditional inn or restaurant — more specific to the hospitality industry and carries connotations of traditional Japanese service
- {主人|しゅじん}: master, proprietor — typically refers to a male owner or husband
- {亭主|ていしゅ}: husband, master of the house — informal, can also mean male innkeeper
